# Mainframe metric refinements

Metric refinements extend upstream OpenTelemetry metrics with additional
entity associations and attributes specific to the
Mainframe domain.

| Upstream Metric | Refinement ID | Entity Associations | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `system.network.errors` | `refinement.mainframe.nic.system.network.errors` | mainframe.partition.nic | Count of network errors detected on the partition virtual NIC. |
| `system.network.io` | `refinement.mainframe.nic.system.network.io` | mainframe.partition.nic | Network bytes transmitted and received through the partition virtual NIC. |
| `system.network.packet.count` | `refinement.mainframe.nic.system.network.packet.count` | mainframe.partition.nic | Network packets transferred through the partition virtual NIC. |
| `system.network.packet.dropped` | `refinement.mainframe.nic.system.network.packet.dropped` | mainframe.partition.nic | Network packets dropped on the partition virtual NIC. |
| `system.network.errors` | `refinement.mainframe.port.system.network.errors` | mainframe.adapter.port | Count of network errors detected on the mainframe physical adapter port. |
| `system.network.io` | `refinement.mainframe.port.system.network.io` | mainframe.adapter.port | Network bytes transmitted and received through the mainframe physical adapter port. |
| `system.network.packet.count` | `refinement.mainframe.port.system.network.packet.count` | mainframe.adapter.port | Network packets transferred through the mainframe physical adapter port. |
| `system.network.packet.dropped` | `refinement.mainframe.port.system.network.packet.dropped` | mainframe.adapter.port | Network packets dropped on the mainframe physical adapter port. |
| `system.cpu.utilization` | `refinement.mainframe.system.cpu.utilization` | virtualization.platform, virtualization.partition | Per-logical-CPU utilization by mode, extended for IBM Z processor specialization. |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.weight` | `refinement.mainframe.virtualization.partition.cpu.weight` | virtualization.partition | Processing weight of the logical partition (LPAR), by IBM Z weight category. |


## `refinement.mainframe.nic.system.network.errors`

Refines upstream metric: `system.network.errors`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `system.network.errors` | Counter | `{error}` | Count of network errors detected on the partition virtual NIC. [1] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `mainframe.partition.nic` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[1]:** Measured as:

- Linux: the `errs` column in `/proc/net/dev` ([source](https://web.archive.org/web/20180321091318/http://www.onlamp.com/pub/a/linux/2000/11/16/LinuxAdmin.html)).
- Windows: [`InErrors`/`OutErrors`](https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/netioapi/ns-netioapi-mib_if_row2)
  from [`GetIfEntry2`](https://docs.microsoft.com/windows/win32/api/netioapi/nf-netioapi-getifentry2).

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.partition.nic.name`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-partition-nic-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The name of the virtual network interface card (NIC) attached to a logical partition (LPAR) in Dynamic Partition Manager (DPM) mode. [1] | `nic-0`; `nic-mgmt`; `nic-prod` |
| [`network.io.direction`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/network.md) | ![Release Candidate](https://img.shields.io/badge/-rc-mediumorchid) | `Required` | string | The direction of traffic from the perspective of the observing host's physical or virtual network interface. It should not be used to represent the logical direction of a stateful connection or network flow. | `transmit` |
| [`network.interface.name`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/network.md) | ![Release Candidate](https://img.shields.io/badge/-rc-mediumorchid) | `Recommended` | string | The network interface name. | `lo`; `eth0` |

**[1] `mainframe.partition.nic.name`:** Reported by the HMC Web Services API partition-attached-network-interface metric group. In distributed systems terms, this is analogous to a virtual NIC (vNIC) attached to a virtual machine.

`network.io.direction` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| `transmit` | transmit | ![Release Candidate](https://img.shields.io/badge/-rc-mediumorchid) |

| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `system.cpu.utilization` | Gauge | `1` | Per-logical-CPU utilization by mode, extended for IBM Z processor specialization. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.platform`; `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`mainframe.cpu.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-cpu-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). [10] | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |
| [`cpu.mode`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/cpu.md) | ![Release Candidate](https://img.shields.io/badge/-rc-mediumorchid) | `Recommended` | string | The mode of the CPU [11] | `user`; `system` |
| [`cpu.logical_number`](https://github.com/open-telemetry/semantic-conventions/blob/v1.44.0/docs/registry/attributes/cpu.md) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Opt-In` | int | The logical CPU number [0..n-1] | `1` |

**[10] `mainframe.cpu.type`:** IBM Z processor specialisation type (cp, ifl, iip, icf, sap, cbp, aap). Maps to HMC CPC and logical partition usage fields.

**[11] `cpu.mode`:** Following modes SHOULD be used: `user`, `system`, `nice`, `idle`, `iowait`, `interrupt`, `steal`

**[12] `mainframe.cpu.sharing.mode`:** Indicates whether the utilization measurement represents shared or dedicated processors.

| `dedicated` | The processor is dedicated to a specific partition and cannot be shared with other partitions. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `shared` | The processor can be shared among multiple partitions and is not dedicated to a specific partition. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

## `refinement.mainframe.virtualization.partition.cpu.weight`

Refines upstream metric: `virtualization.partition.cpu.weight`

| Name | Instrument Type | Unit (UCUM) | Description | Stability | Entity Associations |
| -------- | --------------- | ----------- | -------------- | --------- | ------ |
| `virtualization.partition.cpu.weight` | Gauge | `1` | Processing weight of the logical partition (LPAR), by IBM Z weight category. [5] | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `virtualization.partition` |

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**[5]:** The weight determines the proportion of available processor cycles allocated to this partition relative to other partitions when spare capacity is available. Higher weights grant proportionally more CPU time under contention. In IBM Z PR/SM the weight is an integer in the range 1–999 set on the logical partition or partition object via the HMC Web Services API properties `initial-processing-weight`, `minimum-processing-weight`, `current-processing-weight`, and `maximum-processing-weight` (all modes). On IBM Z, the mainframe refinement of this metric adds `mainframe.partition.weight.type` to distinguish the weight categories.

**Attributes:**

| Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`virtualization.partition.id`](/docs/registry/virtualization/README.md#virtualization-partition-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Required` | string | Unique identifier for the hardware or firmware partition. [13] | `LPAR01`; `PRODZ` |
| [`mainframe.partition.weight.type`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-partition-weight-type) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Opt-In` | string | The scheduling weight type that determines how processor time is allocated to the logical partition (LPAR). [14] | `initial`; `minimum`; `current` |

**[13] `virtualization.partition.id`:** Identifies the partition within its virtualization platform (`virtualization.platform.id`); the pair identifies it globally. The value MUST be the same for every observer of the partition. On IBM Z and LinuxONE this is the logical partition (LPAR) name, which the HMC Web Services API, z/OS RMF (SMF type 70 `SMF70LPM`) and Linux on IBM Z (`/proc/sysinfo` `LPAR Name`) all report.

**[14] `mainframe.partition.weight.type`:** Identifies the weight category being reported (initial, minimum, current, or maximum). IBM Z reports the processing weight per category; other platforms report a single weight.

---

`mainframe.partition.weight.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `current` | The current processor weight actively in use by the partition at the time of observation. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `initial` | The initial processor weight assigned to the partition at activation, representing its baseline entitlement. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `maximum` | The maximum processor weight the partition may consume when spare capacity is available. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `minimum` | The minimum processor weight guaranteed to the partition, below which its allocation will not fall. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
